natural_body: SMB 40% discounts lifted acquisition and near-term revenue but cut retention 12%.

first.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and simplifying onboarding is the lever that plausibly moves both while compounding into durable qualified revenue rather than one-quarter acquisition. I am explicitly declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor pressure: memory_73 records a 12% retention hit, which trades directly against the sustainable-revenue objective, and matching an entry-price attack tends to select for the least durable accounts. Referral incentives (memory_57) act on the installed base and do not address the funnel regression; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment than the one bleeding. I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the sole evidentiary basis for my intended action and, as consolidated summaries, may be two restatements of a single underlying experiment rather than two independent confirmations. If the archive shows they share a source, my effective evidence is roughly half what the memory set implies, and if either measured only proxy completion rates rather than downstream retained revenue, the inference to sustainable revenue is weaker than the summary language suggests. Both memories also predate the competitor's entry pricing by 15-64 days, so the population they were measured on may no longer be the population arriving today. I therefore run this as a standard experiment with a retention and revenue-quality guardrail rather than a broad rollout, and I treat the current read as provisional pending the archived records.
